findings.description: The handoff explicitly withholds implementation authorization while the public request requires implementation of a production-ready feature. Material API, capacity, fairness, observability, history, retention, and acceptance decisions remain unresolved.
findings.why_material: Implementation cannot begin without silently choosing behavior that affects public API compatibility, replay amplification, tenant isolation under load, operational support, and the evidence required to call the feature production-ready.

citations.quoted_text: Management API idempotency, validation, pagination, error contract, and compatibility/versioning
Tenant endpoint, event-volume, replay, and worker-concurrency quotas and abuse controls

Force-closed at the runtime safety ceiling. The requested webhook feature is not implementation-ready because material decisions remain unresolved; no unconfirmed behavior has been silently defaulted.

findings.description: The acceptance section consists of instructions to define future tests rather than executable checks with fixtures, actions, and exact expected results. The critical partial-failure interaction requested by the user therefore has no sealable acceptance evidence.
findings.why_material: Component behavior can appear correct while a lost acknowledgement or ambiguous crash produces duplicate business effects, an incorrect terminal state, or incomplete history. The contract itself acknowledges that the required matrices and checks have not been defined.

citations.quoted_text: Not sealable yet: define tests proving atomic business-event and complete fanout commit or rollback, including oversized payload rejection.
Define tests proving lost acknowledgements and ambiguous worker crashes may repeat requests while fenced stale workers cannot overwrite authoritative state.

Define history and replay API acceptance checks after pagination, filters, status presentation, idempotency, validation errors, rate limits, quotas, compatibility, and audit-retention decisions are confirmed.

findings.description: Emergency secret revocation cancels scheduled work, but the authoritative state machine provides only cancelled_endpoint_disabled and defines no cancellation state or attempt outcome for secret compromise. The contract also says delivery resumes after replacement activation without defining whether or how already-cancelled runs transition or receive replacement attempts.
findings.why_material: Workers and history implementations cannot consistently record, display, or recover revocation-affected deliveries. Reusing cancelled_endpoint_disabled would report a false cause, while inventing a new state or revival transition would exceed the sealed decisions.

citations.quoted_text: Emergency compromise revokes the secret without overlap, pauses new attempts, cancels scheduled future attempts, and requires an authorized replacement-secret activation before delivery resumes.

Delivery and replay-run states are pending, retry_scheduled, in_flight, succeeded, failed_permanent, failed_exhausted, and cancelled_endpoint_disabled. Attempts record explicit immutable outcomes and transition reasons with timestamps.

Immediately revoke the compromised secret with no 24-hour overlap, pause all new attempts for the affected endpoint, cancel its scheduled future attempts without deleting or rewriting history, and resume delivery only after an authorized operator activates a replacement secret. Existing delivery, replay-run, and attempt records remain immutable and auditable.

review_summary: Three material blockers remain: implementation is explicitly unauthorized because material decisions are open, the acceptance checks are not yet verifiable tests, and emergency secret revocation cannot be represented or recovered under the stated lifecycle model.
